_source: ADR 2.2 — classification code systems per class (API field: classificationCode). This is NOT a 1:1 lookup — the code must be decoded according to the goods' class (hazardClass).

class_1._note: The Class 1 classification code = division (1.1-1.6) + compatibility group letter (A-S), e.g. '1.1D'.

divisions.1.1: Mass explosion hazard (affecting almost the entire load virtually instantaneously)
divisions.1.2: Projection hazard but not a mass explosion hazard
divisions.1.3: Fire hazard and either a minor blast hazard or a minor projection hazard or both, but not a mass explosion hazard
divisions.1.4: No significant hazard beyond the package in case of ignition or initiation — effects largely confined to the package
divisions.1.5: Very insensitive substances with a mass explosion hazard, but with a low probability of initiation
divisions.1.6: Extremely insensitive articles with no mass explosion hazard

compatibility_groups.B: Article containing a primary explosive substance and not having two or more effective protective features (e.g. detonators, primers)
compatibility_groups.C: Propellant explosive substance or other deflagrating explosive substance, or article containing such a substance
compatibility_groups.D: Secondary detonating explosive substance or black powder (without its own means of initiation and without a propelling charge), or article containing a primary explosive substance and having two or more effective protective features
compatibility_groups.E: Article containing a secondary detonating explosive substance, without its own means of initiation, with a propelling charge (other than one containing flammable liquid, gel or hypergolic liquids)
compatibility_groups.F: Article containing a secondary detonating explosive substance with its own means of initiation, with a propelling charge (other than one containing flammable liquid or gel or hypergolic liquids) or without a propelling charge
compatibility_groups.G: Pyrotechnic substance, or article containing a pyrotechnic substance, or article containing both an explosive substance and an illuminating, incendiary, tear- or smoke-producing substance
compatibility_groups.H: Article containing both an explosive substance and white phosphorus
compatibility_groups.J: Article containing both an explosive substance and a flammable liquid or gel
compatibility_groups.K: Article containing both an explosive substance and a toxic chemical agent
compatibility_groups.L: Explosive substance or article containing an explosive substance presenting a special risk (e.g. water-activated, hypergolic liquids, phosphides, pyrophoric substances) requiring isolation of each type
compatibility_groups.N: Articles containing predominantly extremely insensitive detonating substances
compatibility_groups.S: Substance or article packaged or designed so that any hazardous effects of accidental functioning are confined within the package

class_2._note: Groups by hazardous properties (excluding aerosols and pressurized chemicals under separate special provisions).

class_3.F: Flammable liquids, with no subsidiary hazard
class_3.F2: Flash point > 60°C, carried or offered for carriage at or above their flash point (elevated temperature)

class_4_1.F: Flammable solids, with no subsidiary hazard
class_4_1.D: Desensitized solid explosives, with no subsidiary hazard

class_4_2.S: Substances liable to spontaneous combustion, with no subsidiary hazard
class_4_2.SW: Liable to spontaneous combustion, emitting flammable gases in contact with water

class_4_3.W: Emits flammable gases in contact with water, with no subsidiary hazard

class_5_1.O: Oxidizing substances, with no subsidiary hazard
class_5_1.OW: Solid, emitting flammable gases in contact with water

class_5_2.P1: Organic peroxides not requiring temperature control

class_6_1.TW: Toxic, emitting flammable gases in contact with water
class_6_1.TFW: Toxic, flammable, emitting flammable gases in contact with water

class_7._note: Deliberately excluded from analyses — exceptionally complex class (per source guidance); model responses limited in scope.

class_8.C1_C4: Acidic substances (C1 inorganic liquid, C2 inorganic solid, C3 organic liquid, C4 organic solid)
class_8.C5_C8: Basic substances (C5 inorganic liquid, C6 inorganic solid, C7 organic liquid, C8 organic solid)
class_8.CW: Corrosive, emitting flammable gases in contact with water

class_9.M1: Substances inhaled as fine dust that may endanger health
class_9.M2: Substances/articles which, in case of fire, may form dioxins
class_9.M11: Other substances/articles presenting a danger during carriage but not meeting the other definitions
